Package de.labathome.trustconstr.sparse

Class CSRMatrix

java.lang.Object
de.labathome.trustconstr.sparse.CSRMatrix
public final class CSRMatrix extends Object
Compressed Sparse Row matrix. Storage analogue of scipy.sparse.csr_array: three parallel primitive arrays (indptr, indices, data) together with the logical shape. 
 indptr.length == rows + 1
 indptr[i] .. indptr[i+1] is the half-open range of indices/data
     entries belonging to row i.
 indices[k] is the column of the k-th stored entry (0 ≤ indices[k] < cols).
 data[k]    is the value of the k-th stored entry.
Within a row the entries are kept sorted by column index -- this matches the canonical form scipy returns from csr_array(...) after sum_duplicates() / sort_indices(), and several operations (e.g. toDense(), matvec(double[])) rely on it being safe to walk the row range linearly. Instances are immutable from the outside: the constructor copies its inputs.

  • Constructor Details

    • CSRMatrix

      public CSRMatrix(int rows, int cols, int[] indptr, int[] indices, double[] data)
      Construct from raw CSR triplets. Inputs are defensively copied. The arrays must satisfy:
      • indptr.length == rows + 1, monotonically non-decreasing, starting at 0 and ending at indices.length.
      • indices.length == data.length (the number of stored entries).
      • 0 <= indices[k] < cols for every k.
      • Within each row, indices is strictly increasing.
      Parameters:
      rows - number of rows
      cols - number of columns
      indptr - row pointer array, length rows + 1
      indices - column index for each stored entry
      data - value for each stored entry

    • transpose

      public CSCMatrix transpose()
      Transpose: returns a CSC matrix with the same non-zeros, rows/columns swapped. CSC is the natural output because a CSR row traversal of A is a CSC column traversal of A^T.
      Returns:
      A^T as a CSCMatrix
